sections.risk_rationale: Guideline mandates starting with a personal story of encountering the problem, specific open-book exam and fine-tuning analogies, plus Lesson 10 memory contrast, which carry motivational/normative framing weight beyond the purely descriptive motivation coverage in sources like rag-fundamentals-first-by-paul-iusztin-decoding-ml.
Purely descriptive breakdown of retrieval/augmentation/generation pillars and Mermaid diagram per guideline, well-supported by sources with low interpretive leaps.
Guideline scripts two-phase pipeline steps with generic tool references and dual Mermaid diagram, but remains descriptive of standard workflow with minimal normative claims or unsupported analogies.

Guideline dictates multiple specific invented examples (travel policy decomposition, retail/IT GraphRAG multi-hop, pricing table chunking) and What/Why rationales for hybrid/re-ranking/HyDE that are illustrative narratives not directly evidenced in the cited advanced-rag-blueprint sources.

Guideline provides verbatim mini thought-process example (Thought/Action/Observation on EU data retention) plus core distinction claims about adaptive superiority over linear RAG and ties to ReAct (Lessons 7-8), which carry interpretive weight on agent capabilities with only partial support from what-is-agentic-rag sources and a high-level preview of Lesson 10 memory.

Section makes normative claims positioning RAG as 'foundational competency for the modern AI Engineer' and 'most used solution' within Context Engineering, plus previews of Lesson 10 and later evaluations/monitoring, going beyond purely descriptive summary supported by the-rise-of-rag and a-complete-guide-to-rag.

parsed.overall_notes: RAG is a highly canonical, well-saturated topic (original 2020 paper plus dozens of near-identical pipeline explanations across NVIDIA, decodingml, Weaviate, IBM etc.), yielding mostly redundant coverage despite distinct documents like the GraphRAG arXiv paper; this plus the 100% theory guideline with many pre-scripted analogies/examples (esp. S4/S5) and course-specific normative framing explain why numeric depth/breadth gaps overstate the value of further exploration.
